tool.name: HUMAnN download
tool.help:
**What this tool installs**
The three HUMAnN reference data tables that the HUMAnN tools select from:
| Table | Data | Used for | | --- | --- | --- | | ``humann_nucleotide_database`` | ChocoPhlAn pangenome catalog | nucleotide (bowtie2) search, and the catalog the per-sample pangenome is built from | | ``humann_protein_database`` | UniRef protein clusters | translated (DIAMOND) search | | ``humann_utility_mapping`` | feature to group / to name mappings | ``humann_regroup_table``, ``humann_rename_table`` |
**Data versions live in the artifact names, not in the HUMAnN version**
HUMAnN names each bundle after the data it contains. Query them with ``humann_databases --available``:
- ``full_chocophlan.v201901_v31`` (chocophlan, full) http://huttenhower.sph.harvard.edu/humann_data/chocophlan/full_chocophlan.v201901_v31.tar.gz - ``DEMO_chocophlan.v201901_v31`` (chocophlan, DEMO) http://huttenhower.sph.harvard.edu/humann_data/chocophlan/DEMO_chocophlan.v201901_v31.tar.gz - ``uniref90_annotated_v201901b_full`` (uniref, uniref90_diamond) http://huttenhower.sph.harvard.edu/humann_data/uniprot/uniref_annotated/uniref90_annotated_v201901b_full.tar.gz - ``full_mapping_v201901b`` (utility_mapping, full) http://huttenhower.sph.harvard.edu/humann_data/full_mapping_v201901b.tar.gz
**These are the same for every HUMAnN from 3.1.1 to 3.9** — the ChocoPhlAn ``v201901_v31`` catalog and the UniRef/mapping ``201901b`` bundle. Upgrading HUMAnN between those releases does not require downloading anything again, and HUMAnN validates this: it refuses to run if the data directory contains a file that does not carry the expected version string.
The one exception is **HUMAnN 3.0.x**, which shipped ``chocophlan.v296_201901b``. That cohort is only usable with HUMAnN 3.0.x; every later release aborts with ``CRITICAL ERROR: The directory provided for ChocoPhlAn contains files ... that are not of the expected version``. The HUMAnN wrappers therefore only offer nucleotide databases whose entries mention ``v201901_v31``.
A future HUMAnN 4 uses a new generation (``chocophlan.v4_alpha``, ``uniref90_annotated_v4_alpha_ec_filtered``, ``full_mapping_v4_alpha``) with fewer variants (no UniRef50, no DEMO); those bundles are not offered to the current wrappers.
The **MetaPhlAn marker database** used for the prescreen step is separate data (the ``metaphlan_database_versioned`` table, installed by the MetaPhlAn data manager) and is versioned independently. HUMAnN accepts:
| HUMAnN | Accepted marker database | | --- | --- | | 3.1.1 | ``mpa_v30_CHOCOPhlAn_201901`` | | 3.5 - 3.6.1 | ``mpa_v30_CHOCOPhlAn_201901``, ``mpa_vJan21_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202103`` | | 3.7 - 3.8 | ``mpa_v30_CHOCOPhlAn_201901``, ``mpa_vOct22_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202212`` | | 3.9 | ``mpa_v30_CHOCOPhlAn_201901``, ``mpa_vJun23_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202307``, ``mpa_vJun23_CHOCOPhlAnSGB_202403`` |
Rows holding a pre-v3 (``legacy``) database must be marked as such in the ``db_version`` column of ``metaphlan_database_versioned``, so that HUMAnN is called with ``--mpa3``. The ``humann`` conda package also pins ``metaphlan >=4.0,<4.2``, because MetaPhlAn 4.2 renamed the command line flags that HUMAnN's prescreen step uses.
**Columns**
``value`` Stable identity of the data, ``<database>-<build>-<artifact name>`` (for mappings additionally the mapping file name). It never contains an install date: workflows serialize this value, so it has to be identical on every Galaxy instance. The managed path is derived from it. ``name`` Human readable label, as shown in the tool form, with the artifact name in parentheses. ``dbkey`` The HUMAnN version the entry was installed for. This is provenance, **not** a data version — the data does not change between HUMAnN 3.1.1 and 3.9. ``path`` Absolute path of the database directory (or of the mapping file) on this server.
**Adding data by hand**
Install the bundle with ``humann_databases --download <database> <build> <target dir> --update-config no`` and add a row whose ``value`` follows the scheme above (the artifact name is the tarball name without the archive suffix). The directory must contain the files unmodified — HUMAnN checks the version strings in the file names. The ``DEMO`` bundles are reduced test data and are not suitable for real analyses.
**Re-installing**
The target path is derived from ``value``, so installing the same database and build twice produces the same entry and the same directory. Remove the existing entry first if you need to replace it.
Read more about the tool at http://huttenhower.sph.harvard.edu/humann .
